item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00290","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C11","C05","C12"],"selected_candidate_label":"C11","confidence":0.84,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C11 plausibly supplied a material argumentative and drafting structure: identify worthwhile water projects within a broader authorization bill, distinguish authorization from the later availability of construction funds, object that important policy questions require additional executive-branch study, and explain that deferral will not materially delay construction because Congress can act after receiving fully considered recommendations. The child adapts this same machinery from one irrigation component to numerous insufficiently reviewed river, harbor, and flood-control projects. C05 and C12 share the narrower water-project rationale that legislation should await completed studies and consultation with affected states or Canada, but they provide a less comprehensive template for the child's veto message.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"This bill does not appropriate funds. It only authorizes certain projects or project-modifications so that the next Congress can consider them for appropriation. So my action on the bill need cause no delay in starting the many worthwhile projects in the bill.","parent_excerpt":"although the irrigation development would be authorized by this bill, the appropriation of funds for that purpose would not be authorized. Consequently, further authorizations would be necessary before funds could be made available for the irrigation development and construction started.","explanation":"Both use the distinction between project authorization and later funding to argue that withholding present authorization will not materially delay construction."},{"child_excerpt":"In the weeks before the Congress convenes a careful, orderly review will be undertaken of those projects and other provisions of the bill which have not been fully studied or reviewed at the present time. This should enable the Congress to base its action on a full knowledge of all the facts involved.","parent_excerpt":"Because of the complex nature of the problems involved, they should have the most careful study before this project is authorized... I am having the various policy questions investigated further within the Executive Branch, and expect to submit fully considered recommendations to the next session of the Congress.","explanation":"The child closely follows C11's sequence of demanding study before authorization, assigning further investigation to the executive branch, and promising a better-informed proposal for the next congressional session."},{"child_excerpt":"the periodic enactment of river and harbor and flood control legislation is an important step in the formulation of a sound Federal program","parent_excerpt":"H.R. 5472, a bill to authorize the Corps of Engineers, Department of the Army, to undertake various river and harbor and flood control projects.","explanation":"Both address omnibus river-and-harbor and flood-control authorization legislation involving Corps of Engineers projects, making the shared procedural structure especially transferable."}]}
